![Russian double-tap strike on shopping center in Kryvyi Rih kills at least 15, injures 130](https://kyivindependent.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.kyivindependent.com%2Fcontent%2Fimages%2F2026%2F08%2Fphoto_2026-08-21-19_19_18_20260821-162150.jpeg&w=1536&q=75)
Editor's note: This story is being updated.
Russian forces launched a daytime drone strike on a shopping center in Kryvyi Rih on Aug. 21, killing at least 15 people and injuring 130 others, including 23 children, local authorities said.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said the drones struck in two waves, with the second strike taking place around half an hour after the first, when rescue services were already responding at the scene.
"An absolutely cynical and vile strike was carried out by the Russians against an ordinary shopping center in Kryvyi Rih," Zelensky said.
Oleksandr Vilkul, head of Kryvyi Rih's Defense Council, said the second strike was carried out by a jet-powered Shahed-type drone, adding that the drones were flying at extremely low altitudes.
The Dnipropetrovsk Regional Prosecutor's Office reported at 9:32 p.m. that 15 people were killed. Vilkul said 130 people were injured, 29 of the which were in serious condition, including five children.
"There are people who have gone missing and cannot be contacted," Vilkul said. "Bloody damn Russian bastards," he added.
Ukraine's Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said Russia was deliberately striking places where civilians gather in broad daylight.
"People came to the shopping center for their ordinary business: to shop, to work, or to spend time with loved ones. For Russia, this makes no difference," Lubinets said.
"The Russian army once again proves that civilians are a deliberate target for it in this war against Ukraine," he added.
![Article image](https://kyivindependent.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.kyivindependent.com%2Fcontent%2Fimages%2F2025%2F10%2Fdnipro-take-1-01.jpeg&w=1536&q=100)
The attacks took place at around 4:30 p.m., according to Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office.
Ivan Vyhivskyi, Internal Affairs Minister, said that in the minutes following the attack on "one of the city's largest shopping and entertainment centers," police and emergency services began evacuating visitors, providing first aid and extinguishing the fire.
Vyhivskyi added that firefighting efforts were being hampered by the constant threat of further strikes and that the fire engulfed a third of the center's total area.
The full extent of the casualties and damage is still being assessed.
The Kryvyi Rih strike came after Russian attacks across Ukraine killed at least six people and injured at least 77 others over the previous day, according to local authorities.
Kryvyi Rih, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, has frequently suffered deadly Russian attacks during the full-scale invasion. On April 4, 2025, a Russian ballistic missile struck an area near apartment buildings and a children's playground in the city, killing 19 people, including nine children, and injuring 75 others.
summary: Russian forces launched a daytime double-tap drone strike on a shopping center in Kryvyi Rih on Aug. 21, killing at least 15 people and injuring 130 others. The second strike occurred roughly half an hour after the first while emergency services were already responding at the scene. Officials reported that numerous victims, including children, are among the casualties and serious injuries.
key_points: A Russian daytime drone strike hit a shopping center in Kryvyi Rih on Aug. 21.
The double-tap attack killed at least 15 people and injured 130 others, including 23 children.
The second strike occurred about 30 minutes after the first while emergency responders were actively working at the scene.
Officials noted that 29 of the injured are in serious condition, and some individuals remain missing.

title: M9 crash: Vigil takes place for four people injured in County Kildare crash
author: Hayley Halpin
content:
![A shot of a car crash site showing a section of closed motorway with many emergency service vehicles on the road and debris from the crash.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/b8ec/live/03589560-9d69-11f1-a07c-85afe5c51b6f.jpg)
The collision occurred on the M9 Northbound at Junction 3 at about 03:00 local time on Sunday
- Published
A vigil is taking place in County Carlow for the family injured in the crash on the M9 in the Republic of Ireland last weekend.
Five teenagers were killed in a head-on crash while they were driving the wrong way down the motorway in County Kildare in the early hours of Sunday.
Three women and a seven-year-old boy remain in hospital where they are being treated for serious injuries.
It is believed the injured family were travelling to the airport to go on holiday when the crash happened.
The vigil is taking place at St Clare's Church in Graiguecullen.
Irish broadcaster RTÃ News reported the church is full and some people have been accommodated in the nearby parish centre where the vigil was live streamed.
Bishop of Kildare and Leighlin, Denis Nulty, said people felt "helpless" and that "words fail".
He thanked the first responders "who were on the M9 for hours last Sunday".
"We also remember the five boys in the [other] car and that's the Christian thing to do," Bishop Nulty said.
Fr John Dunphy said that "when a community comes together in prayer, it gives great strength".
"Since last Sunday morning, our hearts were numb."
Speaking to RTÃ Radio One's Morning Ireland, external programme on Friday morning, Bishop Nulty said the vigil was "hugely important".
"People often at times like this don't know what to do," he said, adding that it was a "very tough day for Carlow and the wider area".
He added that he was "saddened" by the actions of the five teenagers in the lead up to the crash.
The five teenagers who died in the car that was driving the wrong way down the motorway have been named as Joe Carthy from Athy, County Kildare, Alex McCarthy from Carlow, Kamil Pustkowski from Limerick, Jeremy O'Brien and Jack Kennedy.
The funerals of Joe Carthy and Alex McCarthy took place in Athy and Carlow earlier on Friday.
The funeral of Jeremy O'Brien will take place on Monday.
summary: A vigil is being held in County Carlow for a family of four who were seriously injured in a head-on crash on the M9 motorway in County Kildare. The collision, which occurred in the early hours of Sunday, also resulted in the deaths of five teenagers who were driving the wrong way down the motorway. Bishop Denis Nulty and local clergy addressed the community during the vigil, expressing grief and thanking emergency responders.
key_points: A vigil took place at St Clare's Church in Graiguecullen for three women and a seven-year-old boy injured in the crash.
The injured family was reportedly travelling to the airport for a holiday when the collision occurred.
Five teenagers driving the wrong way down the M9 northbound died in the head-on crash.
Funerals for some of the deceased teenagers began on Friday, with more scheduled for Monday.

title: Europe, Canada condemn Israeli plans for new West Bank settlement
author: Al Jazeera Staff
content:
![A Palestinian flag is placed at the site where a Jewish settlers' attack killed 3 Palestinians and injured 7 others on March 8, in the village of Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on March 12, 2026. Excluding Israeli-annexed east Jerusalem, more than 500,000 Israelis live in West Bank settlements and outposts, which are illegal under international law. \[Zain Jaafar/AFP\]](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/AFP__20260312__A2ZG4BN__v2__HighRes__PalestinianIsraelConflict-1773665285.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Israeli plans to build a major new illegal settlement that would cleave the occupied West Bank in two have provoked widespread condemnation from around the world.
In a joint statement issued on Thursday, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Canada and Norway called Israel’s opening of construction tenders for more than 1,200 housing units under the E1 settlement project “unacceptable” and in violation of “the territorial contiguity of the Palestinian Territories”.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Palestinians, UK condemn Israel’s ‘destructive’ E1 settlement plan
- list 2 of 4Analysis: Israel’s government can’t disown West Bank settler violence
- list 3 of 4Israel election pressure fuels settlement push as West Bank violence surges
- list 4 of 4‘Badge of honour’: Israeli settlers shrug off global condemnation
The group warned of “legal and reputational consequences” for participants and urged Israel “to retract these plans immediately and end its expansion of settlements in the West Bank”.
“Not only will they take us further from peace, but they further undermine Israel’s international standing,” the statement added.
Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas on Friday welcomed the joint statement and called for an immediate reversal of Israel’s E1 settlement plan and an end to settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank.
He welcomed the seven countries’ reaffirmation that Israeli settlements in occupied Palestinian territory are illegal and undermine the so-called “two-state solution”, and their warning that the plans are a threat to prospects to peace and the territorial contiguity of the Palestinian territory.
Abbas described the E1 plan as representing a highly dangerous step in settlement expansion and annexation, and called on the countries, along with the EU and United Nations Security Council, to enact concrete measures to stop its implementation.
The Egyptian Foreign Ministry earlier also expressed its “complete rejection of attempts to entrench the status quo through illegal settlement expansion” and called on the international community to “take serious steps to stop these violations”.
Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim wrote on social media that the plans “gravely undermine the prospect of a contiguous Palestinian homeland”.
Israel has abandoned “even the pretence of seeking peace or respecting the will of the international community”, he added.
The UN has also condemned the plan. The UN secretary-general’s spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said Antonio Guterres was “deeply alarmed by the reports of new illegal Israeli settlement outposts in the occupied West Bank”, including the new tenders.
Rising violence
Israeli settlements and outposts in the occupied territory are illegal under international law, but their development has accelerated since the start of the Israeli government’s genocidal war on Gaza launched in October 2023.
The project, slated to include at least 3,400 units, would connect occupied East Jerusalem to the Maale Adumim settlement area on roughly 12 square kilometres (4.6sq miles) of Palestinian land.
The settlement would bisect the West Bank from north to south, cutting off the West Bank’s link to East Jerusalem, which for years Palestinians have cited as the preferred capital of their future state.
Israel gave final approvals to the E1 plan last August, with hardline Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich hailing it as “historic”.
“The Palestinian state is being erased from the table not with slogans but with actions,” he boasted.
At least 21 countries condemned the plans at the time.
Israel’s decision to move forward with the expansion comes as rights groups warn of the mass displacement of Palestinians from the West Bank amid rising settler attacks and the growth of illegal settlements.
Research from the UN’s humanitarian body has found that more Palestinians were forcibly displaced by settler attacks, demolitions and evictions in the first four months of 2026 than in all of 2025.
Dozens of Palestinian communities in the West Bank are now at risk of erasure, Human Rights Watch said in a recent report.
Analysts have linked the scramble for settlements to Israel’s upcoming elections in October.
summary: Israel's plans to build a major new settlement under the E1 project in the occupied West Bank have triggered widespread international condemnation. In a joint statement, several Western nations and Canada warned that the housing tenders violate Palestinian territorial contiguity and threaten prospects for peace. Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas welcomed the condemnation, while the UN and other nations also criticized the move amid rising settler violence and displacement.
key_points: The UK, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Canada, and Norway condemned Israel's E1 settlement tenders as unacceptable.
The E1 project involves building housing units that would bisect the occupied West Bank and cut off its link to East Jerusalem.
Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas called for an immediate reversal of the settlement plan.
The UN secretary-general and several countries, including Egypt and Malaysia, also strongly condemned the expansion.
Israeli settlements in the occupied territory are considered illegal under international law.

title: Imran Khan ‘being tortured in prison’
author: Samaan Lateef
content:
![Imran Khan](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/21/TELEMMGLPICT000498779945_17873029258150_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqVzuuqpFlyLIwiB6NTmJwSX5rhseiWKOo9p9OQ-ymek.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Imran Khan](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/21/TELEMMGLPICT000498779945_17873029258150_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqVzuuqpFlyLIwiB6NTmJwSX5rhseiWKOo9p9OQ-ymek.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Imran Khan is being tortured in jail, his sister has claimed.
The former prime minister of Pakistan was moved back to prison on Friday after doctors declared him medically fit during a court-ordered examination, the government said.
“He told me he is being subjected to torture. His one eye was blindfolded. He was repeatedly saying they are torturing me,” said Dr Uzma Khan.
“He told me to tell people outside that they are being unjust to me, they don’t listen to me, these are not humans.”
Sayed Zulfikar Bukhari, Mr Khan’s spokesman, repeated the claims, saying: “He is being subjected to repeated torture and severe psychological pressure inside Adiala jail,” he said.
![Dr Uzma Khan, left, speaks with Faisal Sultan, Mr Khan's personal doctor, during a press conference in Islamabad on Friday](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/21/TELEMMGLPICT000499016391_17873029031140_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqVzuuqpFlyLIwiB6NTmJwSX5rhseiWKOo9p9OQ-ymek.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The former international cricketer was taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences under heavy security overnight on Thursday and Friday before being sent back to Adiala jail at around 1am BST on Friday.
Attaullah Tarar, Pakistan’s information minister, said doctors including an ophthalmologist, cardiologist and physician had examined Mr Khan in detail and found him “medically fit”.
On Tuesday, the supreme court ordered that Mr Khan be transferred within 48 hours to Shifa international hospital, a private institution, until Sept 17 for medical assessment after concerns were raised about his health.
The court also ordered authorities to facilitate his meeting with family members, which he had not been able to do in months.
Instead of Shifa international hospital, however, Mr Tarar said Mr Khan was taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences, where doctors from Shifa hospital were present, and was returned to prison within hours.
![On Tuesday, the supreme court ordered that Mr Khan be transferred to Shifa international hospital](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/21/TELEMMGLPICT000499007983_17873028768360_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq3480UNUU8UfSxDSaY1n7MP4Xpit_DMGvdp2n7FDd82k.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Mr Khan’s sister was present during the examination, Mr Tarar said. She also visited him in prison on Tuesday night.
It was the most significant reprieve Mr Khan has received from the courts since he was jailed in 2023 on corruption charges, which he said were politically motivated.
His health has become a growing concern for his party and family. In February, his son Kasim Khan told The Telegraph he had been informed that his father had lost most of the vision in his right eye, with only 15 per cent remaining.
He attributed his father’s health problems to medical neglect and “deliberate denial of proper treatment in jail”, and accused the government of locking him in “a death cell”.
He told The Telegraph last year: “He has been kept in solitary confinement in a death cell with zero transparency. There have been no phone calls, no meetings and no proof of life.”
![The family and doctor of Khan](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/21/TELEMMGLPICT000499015149_17873029024331_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqRo0U4xU-30oDveS4pXV-Vv4Xpit_DMGvdp2n7FDd82k.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The government disputes the allegations.
Mr Khan was removed from power in a 2022 no-confidence vote and jailed in May 2023. He has been embroiled in more than 150 criminal cases, most of which have been dropped.
He is serving 14 years in prison for a corruption case in which he and his wife, Bushra Bibi, were accused of receiving land as a bribe from a real estate tycoon through a trust they had set up while he had been in office.
Prosecutors say the Al-Qadir Trust was a front for Mr Khan to illegally receive land from the businessman. Mr Khan and Ms Bibi pleaded not guilty to the charges, while Mr Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party said the land was not for personal gain and was for the educational institution the former prime minister set up.
Mr Khan continues to command a devoted following, and his jailing has continued to fuel protests by his supporters, who accuse Pakistan’s military establishment of orchestrating his political downfall.
In March 2024, a UN working group termed Mr Khan’s detention arbitrary and politically motivated.
Mr Khan’s sons have urged Dr Alice Edwards, a UN special rapporteur on torture, to investigate his case and press the Pakistani government to cease any further torture or ill-treatment of their father immediately.
The Telegraph has approached the Pakistani government for comment.
summary: Imran Khan's sister and spokesman have claimed that the former Pakistani prime minister is being subjected to torture and severe psychological pressure inside Adiala jail. The claims emerged after Khan was examined by doctors, declared medically fit, and returned to prison following a court-ordered medical assessment. The government has disputed these allegations of torture.
key_points: Dr Uzma Khan claimed her brother stated he was being tortured and blindfolded in prison.
The government stated that a medical examination found Mr Khan to be medically fit before he was sent back to Adiala jail.
Mr Khan has been jailed since 2023 on corruption charges, which he and his supporters maintain are politically motivated.
His family has previously raised concerns regarding his health, medical neglect, and solitary confinement.

title: Why Israeli tenders for illegal E1 West Bank settlement prompted outrage
author: Caolán Magee
content:
![UNSPECIFIED, ISRAEL - AUGUST 22: A view over the separation wall, the Arab village of Al-Eizariya, and The Jewish city of M'aale Adomim, near where the Israeli government plans to build a new neighborhood as part of E1 settlement project on August 22, 2025 in near Jerusalem, Israel. On Wednesday Israel approved plans put forward by far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich that would see a new Israeli settlement of 3,400 homes built east of Jerusalem in the E1 zone, effectively bisecting much of the occupied West Bank. Until now construction in the area has been prohibited for two decades, and is considered illegal under international law. The move has been condemned by the international community, with critics accusing Israel of sabotaging any prospect of a future two-state solution. (Photo by Amir Levy/Getty Images)](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/getty_68bac0c321-1757069507.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Israel has opened tenders for the construction of 1,234 Israeli homes in the occupied West Bank, advancing a major illegal settlement expansion which rights groups say will, in effect, sever Palestinian territory in two.
The move is part of Israel’s plan to create the so-called “E1” area on a stretch of Palestinian land, ultimately creating a continuous Israeli settlement “corridor” between occupied East Jerusalem and the large settlement of Ma’ale Adumim, 7km (4.5 miles) east of Jerusalem. This would further disrupt Palestinian movement between the northern and southern West Bank, and isolate communities on each side. It is illegal under international law.

Ubai al-Aboudi, a Palestinian human rights advocate, told Al Jazeera the project would put a “final nail in the coffin of the two-state solution” and “make the establishment of a Palestinian state impossible”.
The United Nations Human Rights Office has previously described the E1 project as a “grave and unlawful step to consolidate annexation”, while the UN secretary-general has said settlement construction there violates international law and runs directly counter to UN resolutions.
The move has prompted condemnation from several Western governments, which have urged Israel to withdraw the tenders and warned companies against bidding, while Israeli NGO Ir Amim said they were published despite an ongoing legal challenge that could determine the project’s future. Here is what we know.
How have plans for E1 developed?
Plans for E1, short for “East 1” – the Israeli administrative name for the area – originated under Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir in 1991 and were advanced under Yitzhak Rabin in 1994, but residential construction has repeatedly been halted amid international pressure.
Israel began preliminary infrastructure work for E1 in 2004 and later built roads and a police headquarters there, but plans for thousands of homes remained on hold as successive US and European governments warned that construction would threaten the territorial integrity of a future Palestinian state. Israel again postponed advancing E1 in 2022 following US pressure.
US President Donald Trump’s second term in the White House, which began in January 2025, has, however, provided Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government with a more favourable political environment for settlement expansion, according to analysts.
E1 has therefore been revived as part of a wider expansion of Israeli control over the occupied West Bank that has accelerated under Netanyahu’s government, which relies heavily on far-right parties that favour settlement expansion.
Far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who also serves as an additional minister within the Defence Ministry, oversees the Settlement Administration, which has extensive powers over land, planning and settlement development in the occupied West Bank.
Smotrich, who lives in an illegal settlement on Palestinian land himself, has explicitly linked construction of E1 to the prevention of Palestinian statehood. When plans were advanced in 2025, he said their approval “buries the idea of a Palestinian state”, while repeatedly describing his wider West Bank policies as a push towards Israeli sovereignty over the territory, which the Israeli government officially refers to as “Judea and Samaria”.
In March 2025, Israel allocated 335 million shekels ($92m) for construction of a so-called “Sovereignty Road”, designed to divert Palestinian traffic away from the E1 and Ma’ale Adumim area to a segregated route.
In May 2026, Israeli authorities demolished about 50 Palestinian shops and businesses at the eastern entrance to al-Eizariya, also known as Bethany, a Palestinian town located on the southeast slope of the Mount of Olives, about 2.4km (1.5 miles) east of Jerusalem, ahead of construction of the settlement-linked road. Bethany is the site of the Tomb of Lazarus, a holy site for Christian pilgrims and local visitors.
The E1 project is seen as part of a wider push for Israeli settlement of the West Bank as a whole. In February 2026, Israel’s security cabinet approved measures expanding Israeli authority in the occupied West Bank, including allowing greater Israeli enforcement in areas administered by the Palestinian Authority.
Bids for the latest E1 tender close on October 19, eight days before Israeli elections scheduled for October 27.
![INTERACTIVE - Occupied West Bank - E1 settlement expansion map graphic-1755168549](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/INTERACTIVE-Occupied-West-Bank-E1-settlement-expansion-map-graphic-1755168549.png?quality=80)
How will E1 affect Palestinian communities?
E1 lies immediately east of occupied East Jerusalem and the illegal Ma’ale Adumim settlement.
Israel plans to expand Ma’ale Adumim into E1 with 3,400 settlement homes on about 12 square kilometres (4.6 square miles) of Palestinian land there. The wider development also envisages hotels and roads linking the settlement more quickly to Jerusalem.
The latest tender, opened by Israel’s Ministry of Construction and Housing, covers 1,234 homes under one of two construction plans approved for E1.
E1’s location has made it particularly contentious. Ma’ale Adumim and the surrounding settlement bloc extend deep into the occupied West Bank towards the Jordan Valley, with the development threatening Palestinian communities already living on the land there.
About 3,700 Palestinians, predominantly Bedouin, live across 18 communities in the area and have already suffered home demolitions, displacement and restrictions to basic services.
Among them is Khan al-Ahmar, a Bedouin village located directly in the path of the E1 corridor that has faced a longstanding threat of demolition and forcible displacement.
The tender has also been opened while a legal challenge remains before the Jerusalem District Court, according to Israeli NGO Ir Amim.
It said a petition brought on behalf of Palestinian residents, along with Ir Amim, Peace Now and Bimkom remains pending, with the court ordering the Israeli state in June to submit a detailed response by September 1.
Ir Amim said the government had committed to notifying petitioners before tenders were opened but had failed to do so, saying the decision to proceed while the case remains before the court raises “grave concerns about respect for the ongoing judicial process and highlights the state’s resolve to expedite the process ahead of Israel’s upcoming elections”.
![A general view of the Bedouin village of Khan al-Ahmar, which Israel plans to demolish, seen in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on January 23, 2023](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2023-01-23T114642Z_710006372_RC2BWY9IX4GR_RTRMADP_3_ISRAEL-PALESTINIANS-VILLAGE-1787307439.jpg?w=770&resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
How has the international community responded?
The latest move has prompted joint condemnation from the leaders of the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Canada and Norway.
“The Israeli Government’s decision to publish construction tenders for the E1 settlement project is unacceptable,” they said.
The governments warned that E1 would “undermine the prospect of the two-state solution by driving a wedge through the West Bank and harming the territorial contiguity of the Palestinian Territories”.
They called on Israel to withdraw the plans immediately and took the unusual step of directly warning companies against participating, warning of potential “legal and reputational consequences including the risk of involving themselves in serious breaches of international law”.
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband also announced the UK had summoned Israel’s chargé d’affaires and demanded that the tenders be reversed.
Far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir responded by attacking the British government. “Someone should update Ed that the British Mandate for the Land of Israel ended in 1948 and that Israel is an independent state,” Ben-Gvir wrote on X.
Is international condemnation enough?
Despite repeated statements opposing settlement expansion, Palestinian advocates and rights groups say Israel has faced few meaningful consequences for continuing to change realities on the ground in the West Bank.
The International Centre of Justice for Palestinians has called on the British government to impose an immediate trade embargo on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. A coalition of five groups, including the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, has similarly called for the UK to ban settlement trade and impose further sanctions on Israel.
Palestinian rights advocate Ubai Al-Aboudi said international condemnation has failed to deter settlement expansion. “What we have seen thus far is lip service with little action towards Israel,” he told Al Jazeera. “Israel can live with all the verbal condemnation in the world as long as it’s advancing realities on the ground.”
Pointing to the International Court of Justice’s 2024 finding that there is evidence that Israel may be committing genocide in Gaza, as well as the Geneva Conventions’ prohibition on an occupying power from transferring its civilian population into occupied territory, he pointed out that other countries have obligations not to facilitate or recognise such changes.
“The impunity that Israel enjoys has led to this moment,” he said, “where even the facade of a two-state solution cannot be maintained.”
Co-director of the Palestine Institute for Public Diplomacy, Ines Abdel Razek, told Al Jazeera that international warnings about the threat to a two-state solution obscured a much deeper failure to act.
“The ‘prospect of a two-state solution’ is little more than diplomatic rhetoric used to cover deliberate inaction and complicity in the decades-long dispossession of Palestinians.
“The Israeli colonial regime has wiped out Gaza, destroyed its schools, universities, hospitals and agricultural land, and rendered two million people displaced and homeless, while continuing its decades-long annexation of the West Bank virtually without interruption. How has that not already killed the two-state solution?” she said.
“The international community has perfected its performance of outrage-crying wolf instead of sanctioning and cutting ties with Israel, thereby further emboldening Israel and entrenching its impunity. We have no illusion that today will be any different.”
summary: Israel has opened tenders for 1,234 homes as part of the E1 settlement project in the occupied West Bank, drawing widespread international condemnation. The controversial project aims to connect East Jerusalem to the Ma'ale Adumim settlement, effectively dividing the West Bank and threatening the territorial viability of a future Palestinian state. Rights groups and international officials warn that the expansion violates international law, while advocates argue that verbal condemnation has failed to deter Israel's actions.
key_points: Israel has advanced the E1 settlement project by opening tenders for 1,234 homes east of Jerusalem.
The E1 project is designed to create a continuous settlement corridor that critics say will bisect the West Bank and undermine a two-state solution.
The move has sparked sharp criticism and joint condemnation from several Western governments, which urged Israel to withdraw the tenders.
Palestinian communities in the area, including approximately 3,700 Bedouin residents, face severe risks of displacement and home demolitions.
Human rights advocates argue that international opposition has amounted to little more than verbal warnings without meaningful consequences or sanctions.

title: Pakistan ex-PM Imran Khan’s family accuses gov’t of defying hospital order
author: Abid Hussain
content:
![Faisal Sultan, personal physician along with sisters of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan addresses a press conference, in Islamabad, Pakistan, August 21, 2026. REUTERS/Akhtar Soomro TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-21T095650Z_1247808416_RC2V2NAMMH1H_RTRMADP_3_PAKISTAN-POLITICS-KHAN-1787307347.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Islamabad, Pakistan — Uzma Khanum had not seen her brother in nearly a year. When she finally did, in a borrowed office in the government-run PIMS hospital in the Pakistani capital past midnight on Friday, he stood up in shock and told the doctors around him, “This is my sister, I’m meeting her after 10 months.”
The country’s Supreme Court had on Tuesday ordered Pakistani authorities to transfer former Prime Minister Imran Khan to the privately run Shifa International Hospital by midnight on Thursday, from Adiala jail, three years after he was imprisoned on a slew of charges.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Pakistan’s Imran Khan back to prison after evaluation at hospital
- list 2 of 4Pakistan’s ex-PM Imran Khan back in jail after brief hospital visit
- list 3 of 4Pakistan challenges top court order to move Imran Khan to private hospital
- list 4 of 4Pakistan top court orders Imran Khan’s hospital transfer amid access battle
But by the time Khanum and Imran Khan’s personal physician, Faisal Sultan, described the night at a news conference on Friday afternoon, it had become, in their account, a story of confusion — marked by what they said was a “failure” by the government to follow the court’s order.
His lawyer told Al Jazeera that, under the order, Khan was to remain there under medical care until the case was next heard on September 16.
Instead, he spent a few hours at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) before being returned to his cell by 5am on Friday, without ever setting foot inside Shifa hospital.
Khan, 73, has been jailed since August 2023 over a series of convictions his party, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) calls politically driven. All but one have since been suspended or overturned on appeal.
Concerns over his right-eye condition, which has required months of specialist treatment, have driven the PTI’s campaign for his release and were central to the medical board report that led the court to order his transfer.
A night of confusion
A journalist who spent the night outside Shifa’s gates, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Al Jazeera the scene appeared designed to convince reporters that Khan would arrive there.
![Police officers block off access to a road leading to Shifa International Hospital after the Supreme Court ordered authorities to move jailed former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan to the hospital, in Islamabad, Pakistan, August 21, 2026. REUTERS/Akhtar Soomro](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-20T210050Z_1139514933_RC2J2NAQTIYU_RTRMADP_3_PAKISTAN-POLITICS-KHAN-1787307434.jpg?w=770&resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
At the first checkpoint on the approach road, only visitors with a hospital card for a patient already inside were being waved through. “You’re a journalist, try the other side,” an officer told him. “We’re not letting anyone through here.”
By the journalist’s estimate, some 400 to 500 supporters of Khan had gathered by nightfall, some having travelled from distant towns in Punjab with their families, convinced the former PM would arrive that night.
At one point, a car pulled up and scattered flower petals on an empty road before driving off.
Barricades went up alongside the hospital. Senior police officers drove past repeatedly with sirens on, while armoured vehicles arrived in what the journalist called a build-up “designed to convince the media that this was, without question, the location”.
For hours, the police inspector-general’s spokesperson gave nothing away. “We can’t confirm that for you,” he told the journalist repeatedly when asked about when Khan would be brought to the hospital. “We’re still waiting for the official word.”
No one asked the journalist to leave, despite a near five-hour wait outside the gate.
The explanation, the journalist said, became clearer later: officials appeared to have calculated that moving the crowd on would only send it looking for Khan elsewhere.
Then, quietly, an official told the journalist, “This isn’t the place, go to PIMS.”
“In hindsight,” the journalist told Al Jazeera, “it is clear we were played.”
Sultan, Khan’s personal physician, gave a similar account at Friday’s media conference.
He said he was driven to Shifa at about 12:30am from Adiala jail and waited for close to three hours, without a phone, while officials repeatedly assured him Khan was “arriving shortly”.
At about 4:30am, he was told Khan was “not going to make it here” and sent back to Adiala. He never saw his patient that night.
Khanum, by contrast, was taken to PIMS, where she said the examination fell well short of what the court had ordered.
There were no blood tests, she said, and doctors treating her brother did not know which eye drops he had been prescribed and had to search his file. Throughout, she said, officials kept assuring her they were still going to Shifa.
Khan himself, she said, repeated the same complaint through the night — that he had been held in isolation for 10 months without reading material or television, and that his blood pressure readings, which he insisted were not naturally high, had been dismissed by jail doctors for months before anyone acted.
“This is what they did to Morsi,” she quoted him as saying, in a reference to Mohamed Morsi, Egypt’s former president, who died after collapsing in a Cairo court following years in detention.
Government’s defence and PTI’s reaction
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said Khan had been examined by “a team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist and a physician,” who declared him “medically fit”, with Khanum present throughout.
![People walk past Shifa International Hospital after the Supreme Court ordered authorities to move jailed former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan to the hospital, in Islamabad, Pakistan, August 20, 2026. REUTERS/Akhtar Soomro](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-20T172933Z_1190844948_RC2H2NAOL9UU_RTRMADP_3_PAKISTAN-POLITICS-KHAN-1787307473.jpg?w=770&resize=770%2C485&quality=80)
He said the switch to PIMS was made because of “the security situation created by PTI workers” on the roads to and around Shifa.
PTI disputed that account in a statement issued by its central media department on Friday, saying it had instructed workers the previous day to stay away from Shifa and noting there were no independent reports of any security disturbance near the hospital that night.
Neither Tarar nor the interior ministry has directly addressed why Sultan, whom the court’s order specifically named as entitled to be present, was kept from the examination.
PTI reacted with fury. Zulfikar Bukhari, a senior PTI leader and a close aide to Khan, said the party would challenge how the government had acted.
“This is a complete violation of the Supreme Court’s orders,” he told Al Jazeera. “There was no thorough check-up. What happened to the medical board? It’s a total sham.”
Faisal Fareed, a lawyer who has previously represented Khan, quoting the order’s requirement that the government act “in letter and spirit”, called the switch to PIMS “an absolute violation” and said Khan’s 10 months in isolation amounted to treatment of a political opponent unseen “perhaps not since the era of British colonial rule.”
PTI’s information secretary, Sheikh Waqas Akram, said the party was preparing to go to the Supreme Court, accusing the government of contempt of court.
“We are filing a contempt petition,” he said, adding that the matter would also be raised in the Punjab state and national assemblies. Adiala prison is in Rawalpindi, which falls in Punjab province.
The party’s statement went further, alleging that sending his physician Sultan to Shifa was itself a deliberate decoy to create the appearance of compliance while Khan was taken to PIMS in a separate convoy.
“Declaring the PTI founder medically fit after a few hours of what appears to have been a merely symbolic exercise and then shifting him back to Adiala jail before dawn raises serious questions,” the party statement read.
PTI’s shifting message
The night’s events landed amid an already tense week for the PTI party’s messaging.
Senior PTI leader Bukhari on Wednesday had told the Reuters news agency that Khan would not confront army chief Asim Munir if freed. But he drew a sharp rebuttal from another senior PTI figure, who said any talk of accommodation with the military was “his [Bukhari’s] personal opinion” and that “the party does not endorse it”.
The leader, who spoke on condition of anonymity, pointed to a message Khan had sent from jail declaring that PTI “will not indulge with the establishment” — a euphemism for the Pakistani military — and said only Khan himself could authorise a change in that position.
The case returns to court on September 16, though PTI’s lawyers say they intend to raise Friday’s events well before then.
summary: Family members and lawyers of jailed former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan accused the government of defying a Supreme Court order to transfer him to a private hospital for medical care. Instead of being taken to Shifa International Hospital as mandated, Khan was briefly examined at the government-run PIMS hospital before being returned to prison. The government defended the move by citing security concerns created by PTI workers and stated that a qualified medical team found Khan medically fit, but the PTI announced plans to file a contempt of court petition.
key_points: The Supreme Court had ordered authorities to transfer Imran Khan from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital by midnight on Thursday.
Khan was instead taken briefly to the government-run PIMS hospital before being returned to his cell by 5 am without visiting Shifa.
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar stated that Khan was examined by a team of qualified doctors who declared him medically fit, attributing the location switch to security concerns.
Khan's family, personal physician, and the PTI party accused the government of violating court orders, staging a decoy operation, and denying proper medical evaluation.

title: Iran war live: Tehran president says it is time to end war ‘in position of strength’
author: Maira Butt
content:
Iran’s president Masoud Pezeshkian has said that it is now time to end the war between Tehran and the US on Friday.
"It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity," Pezeshkian said in a meeting with doctors in the country.
"The whole world acknowledges our victory and emphasises that America has attacked our schools, hospitals and infrastructure in violation of all regulations and is hated around the world."
It comes after Tehran accused US president Donald Trump of threatening "economic terrorism" after the US treasury said it would introduce the “toughest sanctions in history" against Tehran.
Trump has promised to wage "Economic Warfare and Isolation on an unprecedented scale”, suggesting the US will extend sanctions to allies that have helped mediate peace talks.
Meanwhile, over 750 members of the US military have been injured since the Iran war began, US officials said. More than 50 soldiers were added to the Pentagon’s casualty database on Wednesday, bringing the total figures to 757 injured and 18 killed.
Pezeshkian calls for end of war in 'position of strength'
Iran’s president Masoud Pezeshkian has said that it is now time to end the war between Tehran and the US on Friday.
"It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity," Pezeshkian said in a meeting with doctors in the country.
"The whole world acknowledges our victory and emphasises that America has attacked our schools, hospitals and infrastructure in violation of all regulations and is hated around the world."
Beyond the Strait of Hormuz: How Gulf countries are preparing for life without the waterway
As Dubai looks to build a new port and terminal to bypass the beleaguered Strait of Hormuz, it appears that Gulf countries are already preparing for a life without the crucial waterway.
Port operator DP World is in talks to develop new facilities in the coastal area of Fujairah to take pressure off its flagship Jebel Ali port, according to the Financial Times.
Jebel Ali, built in 1977, has made the UAE a hub of finance and trade, but weeks ago it was set alight by a piece of fallen debris from an Iranian missile. Since then, Dubai International Airport, US military bases and other facilities have come under direct attack.
![](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/07/13/23/APTOPIX_Iran_War_Strait_of_Hormuz_29132.jpg?width=1200&height=800&crop=1200:800)
USS Lincoln’s replacement arrives in Middle East after worries over troops’ mental health
The Asia-based USS George Washington aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East to relieve USS Abraham Lincoln following reports of mental health struggles and supply shortages aboard the warship supporting the Iran conflict.
U.S. Central Command confirmed Thursday that the carrier arrived in the region on Wednesday. It remains unclear when the USS Lincoln will return to the U.S. or if it will make a port stop during the journey, which takes slightly over a month.
The Washington's arrival follows growing concerns about the Lincoln's extended tour, which included a record-setting uninterrupted stretch at sea of over 250 days, alongside reports of severe crew strain, poor mental health, and depleted basic supplies such as food and hygiene products.
![](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/20/18/2026-08-19T143103Z_702194656_RC2PZMAOUIBH_RTRMADP_3_IRAN-CRISIS-USA-CARRIER.JPG?trim=0,0,0,0&width=1200&height=800&crop=1200:800)
Teen pleads guilty over arson attack on Iran International offices in London
A British teenager has pleaded guilty to an arson attack on office linked to television station Iran International on Friday.
Nathan Dunn, 19, pleaded guilty to the charge of “arson being reckless as to whether life is endangered”.
The incident took place in April when an ignited container was thrown towards premises belonging to Volant Media, the parent company of the London-based broadcaster.
The device extinguished itself. He had originally been charged alongside a 21-year-old man and a 16-year-old boy who cannot be identified because of his age.
Watch: Trump cannot let Iran make him ‘look like a loser,’ says former Fox News personality
Iran threatens 'devastating response' to US following new threats
Tehran has vowed to deliver a “crushing” response to the US amid threats of economic sanctions.
“With preparedness across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace, Iran's armed forces will respond to the enemy's new threats with crushing, punishing and devastating responses,” chief of staff of Iran;s armed forces, Major General Ali Abdollahi was quoted as saying by Iranian media.
The maps and charts that debunk Trump’s claim the route has reopened
Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has effectively slowed to a halt again despite President Donald Trump claiming the route is open, according to new data.
On Tuesday, the US leader declared the vital waterway “new US territory” in a bizarre post on Truth Social accompanied by a map.
“The Naval Blockade remains in full force and effect,” he continued on the platform. “The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. All water mines have been removed or detonated.”
![](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/18/12/2026-08-18T100559Z_1044002041_RC25ULAU983Z_RTRMADP_3_IRAN-CRISIS-HORMUZ.JPG?trim=0,140,0,140&width=1200&height=800&crop=1200:800)
US Army to shut down unit in Europe focused on drone warfare in latest shakeup
A drone warfare US Army unit in Europe has been told to return to being a traditional infantry battalion.
For more nearly a year, soldiers of the 173rd Airborne Brigade have been experimenting and building their own drones, as well as participating in drills on waging unmanned warfare after Ukraine pioneered such tactics in its yearslong conflict with Russia.
In November, 600 soldiers formed a battalion that specialised in drone warfare and was set up to be used as a dedicated unit that could deploy anywhere drones were required.
Iranian oil offers to Chinese buyers fall as US blockade bites, sources say
Offers to Chinese buyers of Iranian crude have declined and prices have risen this week as a US blockade continues to cut off Tehran’s shipments and the threat of sanctions from Washington, trade sources told Reuters.
The number of offers for Iranian oil cargoes to China for September and October delivery has declined from July and August cargoes, four trade sources familiar with the matter said. The offers have declined as barrels already in ships on the water have been sold, they said.
The US reimposed its blockade of Iran’s shipping and ports on 13 July.
Tehran has condemned the threat of sanctions as “economic terrorism”.
summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that it is time to end the war with the US from a position of strength, while Tehran vowed a crushing response to new US threats of economic sanctions. Meanwhile, Gulf countries are making preparations to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, and the USS George Washington aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln. Additionally, a British teenager pleaded guilty to an arson attack on offices linked to the Iran International television station in London.
key_points: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for ending the war with the US while claiming Iran is in a position of power and dignity.
The US military reported 757 injuries and 18 deaths since the conflict began, while the USS George Washington arrived in the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln.
Gulf countries like Dubai are exploring alternative trade routes and facilities to bypass the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing disruptions.
A 19-year-old British man pleaded guilty to an arson attack on premises belonging to Volant Media, the parent company of Iran International.
Iran threatened a devastating response following US plans to impose severe new economic sanctions and maintain a naval blockade.

title: Pakistan’s ex-PM Imran Khan back in jail after brief hospital visit
author: Al Jazeera Staff
content:
![Security personnel cordon off a street outside the Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad on August 20, 2026 after Pakistan's Supreme Court ordered to transfer jailed former prime minister Imran Khan to hospital for medical treatment.](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/afp_6a87676218f1-1787258722.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Pakistan’s former Prime Minister Imran Khan has been transferred back to prison after a brief stay at a hospital in the capital, Islamabad.
Khan, 73, was moved from Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail to the state-run PIMS Hospital early on Friday, where doctors conducted a medical checkup amid long-running concerns over his health.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Pakistan challenges top court order to move Imran Khan to private hospital
- list 2 of 4Pakistan top court orders Imran Khan’s hospital transfer amid access battle
- list 3 of 4Pakistan’s Khan in jail for 3 years: PTI rallies over ‘arbitrary detention’
- list 4 of 4Clashes on anniversary of Imran Khan imprisonment
The founder of the opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party had been expected to undergo the examination at the privately run Shifa International Hospital, but was taken to PIMS due to a “security situation created by PTI workers,” according to Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.
Earlier, security had been tightened around Shifa ahead of Khan’s expected arrival. A senior official said that hundreds of police and paramilitary personnel had been deployed in the area.
The minister confirmed that Khan was taken to the hospital during the night, where a specialised medical team, including a cardiologist, an ophthalmologist and a physician, examined the former prime minister and “declared him medically fit”. Tarar added that Khan’s sister, Uzma Khan, was present during the entire visit.
The hospital visit followed a Supreme Court order on Tuesday directing authorities to move the imprisoned former leader to hospital within two days. The court said an independent medical board should assess Khan’s condition and include his personal physician.
The court order followed a report submitted to the court on Monday by Adiala jail’s superintendent, detailing an August 10 assessment by a cardiac board. The report recorded fluctuating blood pressure and anxiety that it said was linked to contact with Khan’s family being restricted.
The government had challenged the order, but officials said preparations for Khan’s transfer were completed on Thursday.
Khan’s family and his party have repeatedly appealed to the courts over his health during the past year, particularly concerns about the vision in his right eye.
Courts have twice declined similar requests to move Khan to hospital since February. In one case, the Islamabad High Court instead ordered an assessment by a medical board.
Khan lost power in April 2022 after losing a no-confidence motion in the parliament. He has been in prison since August 2023, when a court convicted him in a case involving the sale of state gifts, charges which he has consistently denied.
The former cricket star and his wife Bushra Bibi have since been convicted in several other cases and have denied all wrongdoing, saying the prosecutions are politically motivated.
summary: Pakistan's former Prime Minister Imran Khan was transferred back to prison following a brief medical checkup at a state-run hospital in Islamabad. The Supreme Court had previously ordered authorities to move the 73-year-old jailed leader for an evaluation amid ongoing health concerns raised by his family and party. A specialized medical team examined Khan and declared him medically fit before he was returned to jail.
key_points: Imran Khan was temporarily moved from Adiala jail to the state-run PIMS Hospital following a Supreme Court order.
A specialized medical team, including a cardiologist, ophthalmologist, and physician, examined Khan and declared him medically fit.
Khan was initially slated for a private hospital, but security concerns raised by PTI workers led to his transfer to PIMS instead.
Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 and faces multiple convictions, which he and his party maintain are politically motivated.

title: Australian hiker's body recovered as police probe error reporting she was alive
author: Harry Sekulich
content:
![Chris Minns speaks at a press conference, wearing a navy jacket and blue collared shirt. He has brown hair with grey tips.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/0161/live/bfab9ab0-9d13-11f1-aa70-15b2bc2a2471.jpg)
NSW premier Chris Minns apologised to Lily Hooper's family after she was wrongly identified as alive
- Published
The body of missing Australian hiker Lily Hooper has been recovered as officials investigate a "miscommunication" that briefly reported she had been found alive.
Within minutes of reports first emerging that she was alive on Thursday, police confirmed that Hooper had been found deceased in the bushland of the Southern Highlands in New South Wales (NSW).
State premier Chris Minns and NSW police commissioner Mal Lanyon apologised to her family on Friday over the error.
Hooper, 18, an experienced hiker, was reported missing last week triggering an eight-day search which involved approximately 1,000 people.
![A blonde woman in a green singlet is pictured in the left. On the right, the same woman is seen sitting on a plane, with her hair in two plaits.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/c439/live/7851db30-9c3b-11f1-853e-ad17ff71705c.jpg)
Lily Hooper, 18, was found dead after an eight-day search in the Australian bush
A police spokesperson confirmed to BBC News on Friday that her body had been airlifted from the Nattai National Park, south-west of Sydney.
"A post-mortem examination will be conducted in coming days to formally confirm ID and determine cause of death," the statement said.
Minns had told a state parliamentary hearing on Thursday that crews had found Hooper alive "with half a bottle of water" eight days after she was reported missing. Within 30 minutes, he corrected himself saying "Lily's body has been found" and she was deceased.
Media outlets in Australia widely reported the initial incorrect reports that Hooper was located alive before retracting their stories shortly after.
The miscommunication meant there was a brief window in which her parents believed she was alive.
Speaking on Friday, Minns said he planned to speak directly to Hooper's family to issue a personal apology.
"The government, myself â we're profoundly sorry", he said.
NSW State Emergency Services commissioner Mike Wassing said that codes are often assigned during major searches.
Such terms can avoid sensitive details being shared over radio broadcasts during a search, when friends, relatives and community volunteers are usually involved alongside emergency service personnel and police officers.
"The codes are usually associated with some aspect like that in terms of bottles of water," Wassing told the Australian Broadcasting Corporation, although he did not confirm the cause of the error which is under investigation.
Lanyon said communications can be challenging during large searches in remote locations.
"Tragically, her condition was miscommunicated, and for that I apologise," he said.
Police will review policy and processes to ensure protocols are "foolproof" into the future, Lanyon added.
![Map of the Sydney region in New South Wales, Australia, showing the location of Nattai National Park. The park is highlighted with a red outline south-west of Sydney and north-west of Wollongong. Labels mark Sydney and Wollongong, while an inset map of Australia highlights the park's location in south-eastern Australia.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/71ff/live/e9348430-9cb6-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.png)
Hooper had been found in the southern highlands, a vast bushland area south-west of Sydney
summary: The body of 18-year-old missing Australian hiker Lily Hooper has been recovered from the bushland of New South Wales following an eight-day search. Officials are investigating a miscommunication after state premier Chris Minns wrongly announced during a parliamentary hearing that she had been found alive. Both Premier Minns and NSW police commissioner Mal Lanyon issued apologies to Hooper's family for the error, which caused them to briefly believe she was alive.
key_points: Lily Hooper, an 18-year-old experienced hiker, was found deceased in the Southern Highlands after an eight-day search involving about 1,000 people.
NSW Premier Chris Minns incorrectly stated at a parliamentary hearing that Hooper was found alive before correcting the statement within 30 minutes to confirm she was deceased.
Premier Chris Minns and NSW Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon apologized to Hooper's family for the miscommunication.
Police are investigating the cause of the reporting error and will review search policies and communication protocols.

title: Lily Hooper’s family was told she’d been found alive. ‘She’s coming home,’ her father said – then tears of joy turned to grief
author: Ima Caldwell
content:
The rugged landscape of the New South Wales southern highlands loomed large on Thursday evening. This country had just revived, then killed hope. A young woman was found “alive”, but then it was confirmed she was dead: desperation, confusion, tragedy reigned.
Here, where the bitumen of Wombeyan Caves Road runs into unsealed dirt, rolling hills dotted with cattle give way to expansive mountains. The late-afternoon sun sends long, beaming rays past the edges of clouds, casting a warm glow on distant cliff faces.
A few hours earlier, after eight agonising days of searchers scouring the Nattai national park, 90km south-west of Sydney, for the missing 18-year-old hiker Lily Hooper, fears had abruptly turned to joy. Police told her family she had been found alive.
Footage from Channel Seven showed the relief and elation. Family and friends embraced, in tears. Her father, Jim Hooper, said “they’re going to get her now by the sound of it … she might be going straight to hospital I’d say”.
He showed off the guitar and packet of Tim Tams he’d brought to the site “because it might lure her out of the bush”.
Her smiling mother, Kirrily, said she had washed her hair and “put my good sneakers on” in anticipation of good news.
There was a toast in celebration.
“I was never going to give up,” Jim said. “She’s a beautiful girl and she’s coming home.”
![The mountains where Lily Hooper went missing.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/ee61722d77d37836a360db0de9f07c4e43dcd8de/0_1476_3024_2419/master/3024.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The NSW premier, Chris Minns, interrupted a grilling in an estimates hearing back in Sydney to announce the discovery about midday, sharing a curious detail that Lily had been found “with half a bottle of water”.
Hope was shattered barely 30 minutes later.
Minns, who had believed he was sharing good news, now interrupted proceedings again.
“I’ve got some terrible news,” he said. “I apologise … Lily’s body has been found.” The bottle of water reference may have been rescuer code – not proof of life.
The SES commissioner, Mick Wassing, on Friday would explain “it’s very common that code words are given to search and rescue crews” to avoid details being overheard by others on radios.
“My understanding is that that’s what has occurred in this situation,” Wassing said.
![The bitumen of Wombeyan Caves Road runs into the unsealed dirt of Wanganderry Road.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/a01f42dadf51b049ea3bdb9277adb5664d0e2ba8/0_0_3780_3024/master/3780.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
On Thursday in the mountains, TV cameras at the site backed away, showing the family embracing, now in grief.
The police commissioner, Mal Lanyon, later told reporters in Goulburn that the devastating miscommunication was “born out of elation”.
“Tragically, that miscommunication then led to a deflation, and obviously, we know now, an impact on her family,” Lanyon said.
Lily, an experienced hiker, had been found dead off the trail, a “significant distance” from her car.
The assistant commissioner Joseph Cassar told reporters in Moss Vale on Thursday afternoon that the searchers had carried handheld radios and faced communication challenges in the “thick, dense terrain”.
Nightfall
As the sun set over the southern highlands command post, the temperature dipped to a bitter chill. By 5.30pm, the sun was gone and the landscape stripped of its warmth, leaving muted greys and browns.
Police said Lily was last seen wearing a T-shirt and shorts, and it was unknown if she had any equipment with her.
The command post, where the search was coordinated, was now still. About 100 Australian Defence Force personnel had joined the operation in the 24 hours before the teenager was located. Almost 1,000 searchers and volunteers had been involved overall.
Emergency workers and volunteers were packing up and driving out on Thursday evening. A NSW Rural Fire Service vehicle slowly towed a trailer back down the dirt road, leaving the command post and passing police cars.
The mourning quiet was broken intermittently by the evening calls of birds and the low hum of idling engines.
A significant presence remained stationed at the operation base. Unmarked four-wheel drives sat alongside SES vehicles, police search and rescue vans, and a large police incident response unit.
The procedures of death were under way. In the distance, a group of officers wearing white jumpsuits gathered.
Hooper’s car had been parked near the trail head on Wanganderry Road at High Range, Cassar said.
The assistant commissioner said it was not yet clear how she died or if she had sustained injuries.
A report was to be prepared for the coroner, investigating the time, place and circumstances of Hooper’s death, in addition to the communications problems.
![A solitary helicopter sits near the dwindling, demobilised search party.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/35c8fd4c4e83a33fb100f2292489ddf84dcdc558/393_1001_3142_1892/master/3142.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
As night closed in, a solitary helicopter sat grounded in a field of tall, brown grass, near the demobilised search party. The last traces of light vanished entirely from the sky.
Then, the whir of a second helicopter overhead broke the silence, touching down at the command post, just as the landscape went dark.
On Friday morning, police announced that Hooper’s body had been winched out of the bush overnight.
summary: Following an eight-day search in the New South Wales southern highlands for missing 18-year-old hiker Lily Hooper, police initially informed her family that she had been found alive. Joy among family members and announcements from public officials quickly turned to grief roughly 30 minutes later when it was confirmed that her body had been found. Authorities attributed the false report to a miscommunication born from elation and potential search-and-rescue code words used over radios in dense terrain.
key_points: Eighteen-year-old hiker Lily Hooper went missing in the Nattai national park for eight days before being found dead.
Police initially told her family she was found alive, prompting public celebrations and joyful statements from her parents.
Roughly 30 minutes later, officials corrected the report, confirming that her body had been located.
Authorities blamed the tragic confusion on a miscommunication and possible rescue code words.
Police stated that a report would be prepared for the coroner regarding the circumstances of her death and the communication issues.

title: UK clashes with Israel over controversial West Bank settlement
author: Kate Devlin
content:
The UK has clashed with Israel over a controversial settlement project in the occupied West Bank.
Ed Miliband , the foreign secretary, called the country’s move to seek bidders to build 1,200 homes as part of the E1 settlement project an “unacceptable and destructive act”. He said the UK would not “stand back and accept the destruction of the two-state solution”.
Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, hit back, accusing the UK of a “patronising tone” and an “absurd” stance.
Mr Miliband said the UK’s opposition to the E1 settlement project, which he said puts the two-state solution at risk by separating the West Bank from East Jerusalem, had been clear both in public and privately.
He said he had told Mr Sa’ar “that the Israeli government must halt E1 plans immediately, retract the tender and stop all settlement expansion”. The Foreign Office also summoned Israel’s chargé d’affaires, the country’s most senior diplomat, to set out the UK’s “profound objection to this move”.
Mr Miliband said the UK remained committed to supporting a two-state solution “as the only way to ensure long-term security and peace for both Palestinians and Israelis. All settlements damage that prospect and are a flagrant breach of international law.”
He added that in the coming weeks the UK would set out a series of measures “to respond to Israeli government policies, protect the viability of the Palestinian state, target sanctions at those who participate in illegal settlement expansion and support a just and lasting peace for Israelis and Palestinians”.
Mr Sa’ar accused Mr Miliband of being “entirely one-sided” and said he rejected his statement and “the patronising tone of his words”.
On X, formerly Twitter, he wrote: “It is absurd for Britain to lecture the Jewish people about where they may live in their historic tiny homeland, when the Jewish people’s connection and right to this land is the most extensively documented of any people in human history.
“There have been no new decisions regarding development in E1. The decision was made on 2025. The tender process has been under way for several months, with certain tender documents published only in recent days.”
Mr Sa’ar said the UK’s policy of “blaming only Israel while ignoring Palestinian extremism” had contributed to antisemitic hatred and attacks against the British Jewish community.
He added: “The UK government’s decision to damage the relationship between our countries is deeply unfortunate. But Israel will not be a passive victim of this policy. Israel will defend its rights, its interests and its people.”
Later on Thursday the UK, France, Germany and Italy issued a joint statement in which they urged Israel to “retract” its plans and warned businesses not to bid for construction tenders.
The statement warned: “International law is clear that Israeli settlements in the West Bank are illegal...At a time of grave instability in the West Bank with unprecedented levels of violence by settlers against civilians, and serious restrictions on the Palestinian economy, this decision is even more concerning.
“We urge the government of Israel to retract these plans immediately and end its expansion of settlements in the West Bank... businesses should not consider bidding for construction tenders. They should be aware of legal and reputational consequences including the risk of involving themselves in serious breaches of international law.”
summary: The UK and several European allies have clashed with Israel over a controversial West Bank settlement project to build 1,200 homes in the E1 area. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband condemned the move as an unacceptable threat to the two-state solution and summoned Israel's chargé d'affaires. In response, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar criticized the UK's stance as absurd and one-sided, while the UK, France, Germany, and Italy issued a joint statement urging Israel to retract the plans.
key_points: The UK condemned Israel's tender to build 1,200 homes in the E1 settlement project as a threat to the two-state solution.
The UK Foreign Office summoned Israel's chargé d'affaires to express profound objection and demanded the plans be halted.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar rejected the UK's criticism, accusing London of a patronizing tone and ignoring Palestinian extremism.
The UK, France, Germany, and Italy issued a joint statement urging Israel to retract the plans and warning businesses against bidding.

title: Five missing after fire in Alpine town in Switzerland
author: Ben Hatton
content:
![Large flames come out of the windows in the top floor of a building at night.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/b130/live/8dbc0170-9d27-11f1-889e-c901b814ac6c.jpg)
- Published
Five people are missing and eight others injured after a restaurant with apartments was "completely destroyed" by fire in the Swiss town of Thusis, police have said.
Initial investigations indicate the blaze broke out on the second floor and the cause was still being investigated, according to the GraubÃ¼nden cantonal police.
The force said it was called just after midnight local time (22:00 GMT on Thursday) and that nearly 100 firefighters responded. The roof had to be opened using a crane after the stairwell collapsed.
The Alpine GraubÃ¼nden region, also known as Grisons, is a popular holiday destination for both winter sports and summer nature activities in eastern Switzerland.
![The building as seen from the air - it is next to a river. Smoke rises from the building at night, while at least five fire engines are parked nearby and on the bridge over the river.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/6419/live/bfd92340-9d27-11f1-ba3e-c323fd3033f4.jpg)
Fourteen people escaped the building, police said, of whom two were seriously injured, two suffered moderate injuries and four suffered minor injuries.
People were taken to hospitals in Chur, Thusis, Ilanz, and Zurich, it added.
Police and the public prosecutor's office are investigating the cause of the fire.
![The building as seen from a bridge crossing a river. Three streams of water from firefighting crews douse the building. Smoke rises from the building - at night.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/c124/live/fe63e140-9d27-11f1-ba3e-c323fd3033f4.jpg)
summary: Five people are missing and eight others are injured after a fire completely destroyed a building containing a restaurant and apartments in Thusis, Switzerland. Police and firefighters responded to the blaze just after midnight, with nearly 100 firefighters tackling the flames. Fourteen people managed to escape the building, and an investigation into the cause of the fire is currently underway.
key_points: Five people are missing following the fire in Thusis.
Eight people sustained injuries and were taken to various hospitals.
Fourteen people successfully escaped the burning building.
Nearly 100 firefighters responded to the incident after being called just after midnight.
Police and the public prosecutor's office are investigating the cause of the fire.
